easy.def: Very, or to a great amount.
examples: I am so happy.
The soup is so hot.
She is so tall.

more.def: To a great degree, or very much.
examples: The night sky was so clear that we could see thousands of stars.
I was so tired after the hike that I fell asleep in the car.
Thank you so much for the lovely gift.

easy.def: A word that tells what happened because of something.
examples: It rained, so we stayed in.
I was hungry, so I ate.
He is sick, so he is home.

more.def: A word used to show that something happened as a result of what was just said.
examples: The bridge was closed, so we took a different road.
I forgot my lunch, so my friend shared hers with me.
The batteries were dead, so the toy stopped moving.

easy.def: To let something sit in water.
examples: I soak the beans.
The rain soaked me.
Soak your feet.

more.def: To leave something in a liquid so that it gets very wet.
examples: I soaked the beans overnight.
The rain soaked my coat.
She soaked her sore feet in warm water.

easy.def: Something you wash with.
examples: Wash your hands with soap.
The soap smells nice.
The soap is slippery.

more.def: A substance that you use with water to wash and clean things.
examples: Wash your hands with soap and water.
The soap made a lot of bubbles.
The bar of soap is on the sink.

easy.def: To fly high in the sky.
examples: The eagle soared.
Birds soar above.
The kite soared.

more.def: To fly or rise high in the air, often without much effort, or to rise quickly.
examples: An eagle soared high above the canyon on the warm air.
The kite soared up into the clear blue sky.
The price of apples soared after the frost killed the blossoms.

easy.def: To cry hard with deep breaths.
examples: The child sobbed.
I sob when I am sad.
She sobbed on the bed.

more.def: To cry loudly and with sharp breaths.
examples: The little girl sobbed when she lost her toy.
He sobbed into his pillow.
She sobbed with joy when she saw her dog.

easy.def: A game where two teams kick a ball into goals.
examples: I play soccer.
We watched soccer.
The soccer ball is round.

more.def: A game in which two teams try to kick a ball into the other team's goal.
examples: I play soccer on Saturdays.
The soccer game was tied at two goals.
She scored a goal in soccer.

easy.def: About being with other people.
examples: A social club.
Dogs are social animals.
Kids are social.

more.def: Having to do with spending time with other people.
examples: Dogs are social animals that like company.
The school held a social event.
She joined a social club.

easy.def: To spend time talking and playing with others.
examples: We socialize at lunch.
Kids socialize at recess.
She likes to socialize.

more.def: To spend time with other people in a friendly way, such as talking and playing together.
examples: Kids socialize at recess by playing games together.
She likes to socialize with her neighbors on weekends.
A puppy needs to socialize with other dogs.

easy.def: People living together.
examples: Society needs rules.
A kind society.
People in society help each other.

more.def: All the people who live together in a country or community.
examples: Society needs rules to keep people safe.
In a kind society, people help each other.
Libraries are important to society.

easy.def: A club or group.
examples: He joined a bird society.
The society meets monthly.
A reading society.

more.def: A group of people who share an interest and meet together.
examples: She joined the local bird society.
The history society meets each month.
The science society hosted a talk.

easy.def: A soft covering for your foot.
examples: Put on your socks.
I lost a sock.
My socks are warm.

more.def: A soft piece of clothing worn on the foot inside a shoe.
examples: I put on warm wool socks.
One of my socks has a hole.
She pulled the socks over her toes.

easy.def: A hole where you plug in something.
examples: Plug it in the socket.
The socket is on the wall.
The light bulb is in the socket.

more.def: A hole or opening that something fits into, such as where you plug in a lamp or screw in a light bulb.
examples: Dad screwed a new light bulb into the socket.
The plug fits into the socket in the wall.
The ball of the shoulder fits into a socket in the bone.

easy.def: A piece of ground covered with grass.
examples: They laid sod on the yard.
The sod is green.
Dad cut the sod.

more.def: The top layer of ground with grass growing in it, cut in squares and laid to make a lawn.
examples: Workers laid sod in squares to make a new lawn.
The farmer cut sod to build the walls of a house.
The new sod was watered every day.

easy.def: A sweet drink with bubbles.
examples: I drink soda at parties.
The soda is cold.
We had soda with pizza.

more.def: A sweet drink that has bubbles in it.
examples: I had a soda with my pizza.
The soda fizzed when he opened the can.
Dad does not let us drink soda every day.

easy.def: A part of salt.
examples: Salt has sodium.
Sodium is in food.
Sodium is a metal.

more.def: A soft, silvery metal that is found in salt and in many foods.
examples: Table salt is made of sodium and chlorine joined together.
Too much sodium in food is not healthy.
Sodium is a soft metal that reacts strongly with water.

easy.def: A long, soft seat.
examples: We sit on the sofa.
The sofa is blue.
The cat is on the sofa.

more.def: A long, soft seat with a back and arms for two or more people.
examples: We watched a movie on the sofa.
The sofa was soft and blue.
The cat napped on the sofa.

easy.def: Not hard.
examples: The pillow is soft.
The kitten is soft.
The bed is soft.

more.def: Pleasant to touch and not hard.
examples: The kitten's fur is soft.
The pillow was soft and warm.
She wrapped the baby in a soft blanket.

easy.def: Quiet.
examples: She spoke in a soft voice.
The music is soft.
A soft sound.

more.def: Not loud; gentle in sound.
examples: The nurse spoke in a soft voice.
Soft music played in the background.
A soft knock came at the door.

easy.def: A game like baseball played with a bigger, softer ball.
examples: We play softball.
My mom plays softball.
The softball team won.

more.def: A game like baseball played with a larger, softer ball and a smaller field, or the ball used in this game.
examples: She plays on a softball team in the spring.
The softball sailed over the fence for a home run.
We practiced pitching and catching a softball.

easy.def: To make or become softer.
examples: Warm butter will soften.
Rain softened the ground.
Her voice softened.

more.def: To make something softer or gentler, or to become softer or gentler.
examples: Leave the butter out on the counter so that it will soften.
The warm rain softened the hard, dry ground.
His voice softened when he spoke to the frightened puppy.

easy.def: In a quiet, gentle way.
examples: She sang softly.
The snow fell softly.
He closed the door softly.

more.def: In a quiet or gentle way.
examples: She sang softly to the baby.
Snow fell softly on the roofs.
He knocked softly on the door.

easy.def: The dirt that plants grow in.
examples: Plants grow in soil.
The soil is wet.
I dug in the soil.

more.def: The top layer of the ground in which plants grow.
examples: The seeds grew in rich soil.
Worms make the soil healthy.
She pressed the soil around the plant.

easy.def: Of the sun.
examples: The solar panels sit on the roof.
We read about the solar system.
A solar light is in the yard.

more.def: Having to do with the sun, or powered by the sun.
examples: Solar panels on the roof turn sunlight into electricity.
The solar system has eight planets that circle the sun.
A solar eclipse happens when the moon blocks the sun.

easy.def: A person in an army.
examples: The soldier wore a uniform.
Soldiers march.
He is a soldier.

more.def: A person who is a member of an army.
examples: The soldier stood guard at the gate.
Soldiers marched in the parade.
My grandpa was a soldier.

easy.def: Only.
examples: She is the sole winner.
The sole survivor.
The sole reason.

more.def: Being the only one.
examples: She was the sole winner of the contest.
The sole reason for the trip was to see the whales.
He is the sole owner of the shop.

easy.def: The bottom of your foot or shoe.
examples: The sole of my shoe is worn.
I have a sore sole.
The sole is rubber.

more.def: The flat bottom part of a foot or a shoe.
examples: The sole of my shoe has a hole.
The soles of my feet were sore after the hike.
The shoe's sole is made of rubber.

easy.def: Hard, not like water or air.
examples: Ice is solid.
The table is solid.
A rock is a solid.

more.def: Hard and firm, keeping its shape, not like a liquid or a gas.
examples: Water freezes into solid ice.
The bridge is solid and strong.
A rock is solid, but the air is not.

easy.def: Something that is hard and keeps its shape.
examples: Ice is a solid.
A rock is a solid.
Solids do not flow.

more.def: A thing that is hard and keeps its shape, not a liquid or a gas.
examples: Ice is a solid, and water is a liquid.
Rocks, wood and metal are solids.
Solids keep their shape when you move them.

easy.def: A card game for one person.
examples: I play solitaire.
Grandma plays solitaire.
Solitaire is played alone.

more.def: A card game that one person plays alone.
examples: Grandma played solitaire at the kitchen table.
You can play solitaire when no one else is around.
He laid out the cards for a game of solitaire.

easy.def: Alone.
examples: A solitary tree stood in the field.
She took a solitary walk.
The solitary bird sat on the wire.

more.def: Being alone, or done alone.
examples: A solitary tree stood in the middle of the field.
She took a solitary walk along the beach.
Owls are solitary birds that hunt on their own.

easy.def: A song or dance by one person.
examples: She sang a solo.
The solo was beautiful.
He played a trumpet solo.

more.def: A piece of music or a dance that is performed by one person alone.
examples: She sang a solo in the school concert.
The drum solo was loud.
His violin solo made everyone clap.

easy.def: Done alone.
examples: It was a solo flight.
She made a solo trip.
He is a solo singer.

more.def: Done by one person alone.
examples: The pilot made a solo flight.
He took a solo trip across the lake.
She is a solo singer who also plays guitar.

easy.def: A way to fix a problem.
examples: I found a solution. We can share the toy!
What is the solution to the math problem?
The solution was to ask for help.

more.def: The answer to a problem or the way to fix it.
examples: The solution to the puzzle was hidden in the last clue.
There is no easy solution to the traffic problem.
The class worked together to find a solution.

easy.def: To find the answer.
examples: Solve the puzzle.
I solved the problem.
She solves riddles.

more.def: To find the answer to a problem or puzzle.
examples: Solve the puzzle by finding the missing piece.
I solved the math problem.
The detective solved the mystery.

easy.def: An amount that is not all and not none.
examples: I want some milk.
Some kids are late.
She ate some of the cake.

more.def: An amount or number of something that is not stated exactly, or only part of a group.
examples: Some birds can fly very long distances without stopping.
I need some paper for my drawing.
We saw some deer near the river this morning.

easy.def: A person, but you do not say who.
examples: Somebody is at the door.
I need somebody to help.
Somebody ate my snack.

more.def: A person who is not named or is not known.
examples: Somebody left a pair of gloves on the bus.
I think somebody is knocking on the window.
We need somebody who can play the drums.

easy.def: At some time in the future.
examples: I will fly someday.
Someday I will be a nurse.
We'll visit Mars someday.

more.def: At a time in the future that is not yet known.
examples: Someday I want to travel to Japan.
She hopes to be a doctor someday.
People will walk on Mars someday.

easy.def: In a way that is not known.
examples: Somehow the cat got in.
We will fix it somehow.
Somehow I lost my hat.

more.def: In some way that you do not know or understand.
examples: Somehow the cat got into the closet.
We will get across the creek somehow.
She somehow knew it was a surprise party.

easy.def: A person, but you do not say who.
examples: Someone is at the door.
I need someone to help.
Someone took my pencil.

more.def: A person who is not named or is not known.
examples: Someone left a bag of apples on our porch.
I need someone to hold the other end of the rope.
Is there someone here who can read this sign?

easy.def: In some place.
examples: I left it someplace.
Let us go someplace fun.
Someplace quiet.

more.def: In or to a place that is not named or known.
examples: I left my hat someplace in the house.
Let's go someplace quiet to read.
They want to live someplace warm.

easy.def: A thing that you do not know or name.
examples: I hear something.
She wants something to eat.
He found something shiny.

more.def: A thing that is not named or not known exactly.
examples: There is something under the bed, and I think it is the cat.
I would like to learn something new about space.
She whispered something to her friend.

easy.def: At a time that is not named.
examples: Call me sometime.
Come visit sometime.
We'll go sometime.

more.def: At a time that is not known or not decided.
examples: Come visit us sometime this summer.
I lost my glove sometime yesterday.
We should go to the zoo sometime.

easy.def: Not always, but now and then.
examples: Sometimes we eat dinner outside.
I sometimes ride my bike.
Sometimes it snows here.

more.def: At some times but not all of the time.
examples: Sometimes the bus is late when it rains.
My grandmother sometimes tells stories about when she was young.
Sea otters sometimes hold hands while they sleep.

easy.def: A little.
examples: I am somewhat tired.
It is somewhat cold.
She was somewhat shy.

more.def: To a small degree, a bit.
examples: I am somewhat tired today.
It was somewhat cold outside.
She was somewhat shy at first.

easy.def: In a place you do not know.
examples: My shoes are somewhere here.
Let's go somewhere fun.
I left it somewhere.

more.def: In or to some place that is not named or known.
examples: I left my hat somewhere in the house.
Let's go somewhere warm for the holiday.
There must be a frog somewhere near the pond.

easy.def: A boy or man who is someone's child.
examples: He is their son.
The baker has a son.
Her son is five.

more.def: A boy or man in relation to his parents.
examples: The farmer and his son fed the cows together.
She is proud of her son, who won the spelling bee.
Their son plays the trumpet in the band.

easy.def: Words and music that people sing.
examples: We sing a song.
The bird's song is pretty.
My favorite song is on the radio.

more.def: A short piece of music with words that are sung.
examples: We learned a new song in music class.
The birds' morning song woke me.
She wrote a song about her dog.

easy.def: A person who writes songs.
examples: The songwriter wrote a tune.
My aunt is a songwriter.
A songwriter visited school.

more.def: A person who writes the words or music for songs.
examples: The songwriter wrote a happy tune about summer.
A songwriter played us her new song on the piano.
He is a songwriter who writes songs for children.

easy.def: Having to do with sound.
examples: A sonic boom is loud.
Sonic waves.
The sonic device.

more.def: Having to do with sound or sound waves.
examples: The jet made a loud sonic boom as it passed the speed of sound.
A sonic toothbrush uses sound waves to clean teeth.
Scientists study sonic waves to learn about the ocean floor.

easy.def: In a short time.
examples: Dinner is soon.
We will go soon.
She will be here soon.

more.def: In a short time from now, or not long after something.
examples: The bus will be here soon, so get your backpack.
Soon after the rain stopped, the sun came out.
I hope to see you again soon.

easy.def: To make someone feel calm or less in pain.
examples: Mom soothed the baby.
Warm tea soothes a sore throat.
The music soothed me.

more.def: To make someone calm and quiet, or to make pain feel less.
examples: Mom soothed the crying baby by rocking him gently.
Warm tea can soothe a sore throat.
The soft music soothed the nervous horse.

easy.def: Making you feel calm.
examples: The music was soothing.
A soothing voice.
Soothing tea.

more.def: Making you feel calm, relaxed or less in pain.
examples: The soft music was soothing and helped the baby go to sleep.
A cup of warm tea is soothing when you have a sore throat.
Her voice was soothing, and I stopped feeling afraid.

easy.def: Fancy and grown-up.
examples: She wore a sophisticated dress.
It is a sophisticated machine.
A sophisticated meal.

more.def: Having a lot of experience and good taste, or being complicated and advanced in design.
examples: She wore a sophisticated black dress and a pearl necklace.
The robot is a sophisticated machine with many moving parts.
The chef prepared a sophisticated meal with many courses.

easy.def: A student in the second year of high school or college.
examples: My cousin is a sophomore.
The sophomore joined the band.
A sophomore won the race.

more.def: A student in the second year of high school or college in the United States.
examples: My cousin is a sophomore, so she has two more years of high school.
The sophomores held a bake sale to raise money for their class trip.
A sophomore on the team scored the winning goal.

easy.def: A person in stories who does magic.
examples: The sorcerer cast a spell.
A sorcerer is in the story.
The sorcerer has a staff.

more.def: A person in stories who uses magic powers.
examples: The sorcerer waved a wand and the room glowed.
In the story, a sorcerer lived in a tall tower.
The sorcerer's spell turned the toad into a prince.

easy.def: Painful when touched.
examples: My arm is sore.
My throat is sore.
His legs were sore after the hike.

more.def: Hurting or painful, especially when you touch or move it.
examples: My legs were sore after the long hike.
She has a sore throat from shouting.
My arm is sore from throwing the ball.

easy.def: A deep sadness.
examples: She felt sorrow.
The sorrow passed.
He felt sorrow when his friend moved.

more.def: A very sad feeling, caused by a loss or a disappointment.
examples: She felt sorrow when her friend moved away.
The town shared its sorrow after the storm.
His sorrow faded as time went by.

easy.def: Sad about something you did.
examples: I am sorry I was late.
She said sorry to me.
He felt sorry.

more.def: Feeling sad or ashamed about something you did, or sad for someone else.
examples: I am sorry that I broke your pencil.
We felt sorry for the lost puppy.
He said he was sorry for being rude.

easy.def: To put things into groups.
examples: Sort the socks by color.
We sorted the blocks.
I sort my cards.

more.def: To arrange things into groups or an order, by color, size or kind.
examples: We sorted the buttons by color and size.
The mail carrier sorts letters before delivering them.
Sort the words in alphabetical order.

easy.def: A kind or type.
examples: What sort of ice cream do you like?
This is a sort of bird.
Which sort of dog is that?

more.def: A kind or type of person or thing.
examples: What sort of music do you like to hear?
This sort of berry grows only in cold places.
He is the sort of friend who always shares.

related.def: A person or machine that sorts things.

easy.def: The deepest part of who a person is.
examples: Music touches my soul.
She has a kind soul.
A song can fill the soul.

more.def: The part of a person that some people believe is not the body, and holds feelings and thoughts.
examples: Many people believe the soul lives on after the body dies.
Music can touch the soul.
She has a kind and gentle soul.

easy.def: Something you hear.
examples: I hear a sound.
The sound was loud.
A bird makes a sound.

more.def: Something that you hear with your ears.
examples: The sound of rain on the roof put me to sleep.
A strange sound came from the attic.
Thunder is a loud sound that travels far.

easy.def: To seem a certain way when you hear it.
examples: That sounds fun.
It sounds loud.
She sounds happy.

more.def: To give a certain feeling when heard or told about.
examples: That plan sounds like a lot of fun.
Your voice sounds hoarse, so you should rest.
The idea sounded silly at first.

easy.def: Not letting sound in or out.
examples: The room is soundproof.
A soundproof room is quiet.
The studio is soundproof.

more.def: Built so that sound cannot get in or out.
examples: The band practiced in a soundproof room.
The soundproof walls kept the noise from the neighbors.
The recording studio is soundproof.

easy.def: A hot food that you eat with a spoon.
examples: I eat soup with a spoon.
The soup is hot.
Mom made chicken soup.

more.def: A liquid food made by cooking vegetables, meat or noodles in water.
examples: The chicken soup warmed us up on a cold day.
He stirred the soup with a ladle.
We had tomato soup and a cheese sandwich.

easy.def: Having a sharp taste like a lemon.
examples: The lemon is sour.
The milk is sour.
Sour candy is tart.

more.def: Having a sharp, tangy taste like a lemon, or having gone bad.
examples: The lemon tasted very sour.
The milk had gone sour.
Sour candy makes your lips pucker.

easy.def: Where something comes from.
examples: The sun is the source of light.
The source of the river.
The source of the noise.

more.def: The place where something begins or comes from.
examples: The sun is the source of heat and light.
A spring in the hills is the source of the river.
We tracked the source of the noise to the attic.

easy.def: The direction that is opposite of north.
examples: Geese fly south for winter.
We drove south to the beach.
The warm beaches are in the south.

more.def: The direction that is opposite to north, toward the bottom of most maps.
examples: Many birds fly south in the fall.
Florida is in the south of the United States.
At noon in the northern half of the world, the sun is in the south.

easy.def: The direction between south and east.
examples: The wind blew from the southeast.
The store is to the southeast.
We drove toward the southeast.

more.def: The direction halfway between south and east, or the part of a place that lies in that direction.
examples: On the map, the lake lies to the southeast of our town.
Many oranges are grown in the southeast of the country.
The storm moved slowly toward the southeast.

easy.def: Toward the direction between south and east.
examples: The birds flew southeast.
Go southeast to find the barn.
The ship sailed southeast.

more.def: Toward the point halfway between south and east.
examples: The explorers walked southeast across the dry plain for three days.
Geese were heading southeast to reach warmer lakes before winter.
Drive southeast for ten miles and you will reach the beach.

easy.def: Having to do with the south.
examples: The southern part of the state is warm.
We drove to the southern coast.
A southern wind blew.

more.def: Found in, from or toward the south.
examples: The southern part of the country is warmer.
Many birds fly to the southern coast for winter.
A warm southern breeze blew over the hills.

easy.def: The direction between south and west.
examples: The wind came from the southwest.
We drove to the southwest.
The southwest is warm.

more.def: The direction that is halfway between south and west.
examples: The wind blew from the southwest.
We drove to the southwest to visit the desert.
The storm moved toward the southwest.

easy.def: Toward the place between south and west.
examples: The southwest corner of the yard is shady.
A southwest wind blew.
We took the southwest road.

more.def: Lying in, coming from or facing the direction halfway between south and west.
examples: The southwest corner of the field is wet.
A warm southwest wind blew all day.
We camped on the southwest side of the lake.

easy.def: Something you keep to remember a trip.
examples: I bought a souvenir.
The souvenir is a shell.
She has a souvenir from Paris.

more.def: A small thing that you buy or keep to remind you of a place or a trip.
examples: I bought a souvenir at the museum.
A shell was my souvenir from the beach.
She keeps a souvenir from every trip.

easy.def: To plant seeds.
examples: Farmers sow seeds in the spring.
I sowed the beans.
We sow seeds in rows.

more.def: To plant seeds in the ground by scattering or putting them in rows.
examples: Farmers sow wheat in the fall and harvest it the next summer.
We sowed lettuce seeds in the garden bed.
She sows flower seeds along the fence every spring.

easy.def: A grown-up female pig.
examples: The sow fed her piglets.
A sow is in the pen.
The sow lay in the mud.

more.def: A fully grown female pig.
examples: The sow nursed her nine piglets in the straw.
The farmer fed the sow in the morning.
A sow can have many piglets at one time.
